description_full: Methode Electronics, Inc. designs, engineers, manufacture, and sells mechatronic products in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. The company operates in four segments: Automotive, Industrial, Interface, and Medical. Its Automotive segment supplies electronic and electro-mechanical devices and related products to automobile original equipment manufacturers directly or through their tiered suppliers. This segment also provides vehicle systems from power distribution solutions, including busbars, smart connect systems, battery disconnect units, and integrated circuit boards, interface components, specialized LED lighting solutions, and advanced sensor applications. The Industrial segment manufactures exterior and interior lighting solutions, industrial safety radio remote controls, braided flexible cables, current-carrying laminated busbars and devices, custom power-product assemblies comprising PowerRail solutions, high-current high-voltage flexible power cabling systems, and powder-coated busbars that are used in various markets and applications, including aerospace, commercial vehicles, data centers, industrial equipment, military, power conversion, telecommunications, and transportation. Its Interface segment provides a variety of high-speed digital communication over copper media solutions for the data networking and broadband markets, and user interface panel solutions for the appliance market; and solutions, including copper transceivers, distribution point units, and solid-state field-effect consumer touch panels. The company serves end markets of transportation, including automotive, commercial vehicle, e-bike, aerospace, bus, and rail; and cloud computing and data center infrastructure, construction equipment, and consumer appliance industries. Methode Electronics, Inc. was incorporated in 1946 and is headquartered in Southfield, Michigan.

financial_summary: Methode Electronics, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $422M market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 1% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $16M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 2.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
